title: B.Sc. in Natural Sciences
description: Students are required to complete a minimum of 51 units of courses as follows: Students must choose one concentration area and take at least 32 units of courses (including at least 3 units of research course(s)) among the subject areas prescribed under required courses and corresponding concentration area courses, namely Biological Sciences, Biotechnology, Environmental Studies, Food and Nutrition, Data Science, Chemical and Testing Sciences, and Physical Sciences. Students will fulfill this unit requirement automatically by taking the relevant courses as prescribed in each concentration area. Also, students shall take no more than 11 units of MATH courses at 3000-5000 level, no more than 10 units from the following CMBI courses: CMBI4001, 4002, 4003, 4101, 4102, 4103, 4201, 4202, 4203, 4301, 4302, 4303, and no more than 15 units from the following PHYS courses: PHYS1001, 1002, 1111, 1122, 2041, 2051, 2401, 3011, 3021, 3022, 3031, 3041, 3051, 3061, 3420, 3730, 4011, 4021, 4031, 4041, 4050, 4051, 4420, 4430, 4440, 4450, 4460, 4470, for the purpose of fulfilling the requirement of this programme. Upon completion of all courses prescribed under a concentration area, the concentration area will be printed on academic transcript.

notes.text: BCHE/BIOL/CHEM/CMBI/EESC/ENSC/ESSC/FNSC/LSCI/MATH/MBTE/NSCI/PHYS/ RMSC/STAT courses at 2000 and above level will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.
These courses if not taken to fulfill the requirement as prescribed in Required Courses can be taken to fulfill the requirement as prescribed in Elective Courses.

Students should take the required number of units of Elective Courses (Item 2) in accordance with the units completed in Required Courses (Item 1) to fulfill the 51 units of courses of Major Programme Requirement.
Students can only use EESC/ESSC2010 or 2020, but not both, to fulfill the Major Programme requirements.
Students taking PHYS1002 instead of PHYS1111 may not be able to take some of the PHYS courses because PHYS1111 is a prerequisite for some Physics courses.
Students may, with written approval by the Natural Sciences Programme, use one or more of the following courses to substitute those listed: MATH2055, 2070, 2230, 3010, 3230, 3240, 4220
